overview: The two broad categories of cells in the body, split by whether they can pass on their DNA to offspring.
genZNote: Somatic cells build the house. Germ cells carry the blueprint to the next generation.

aspects.label: Ploidy
aspects.valueB: Diploid germline cells give rise to haploid (n) gametes.

aspects.label: Passed to Offspring?
aspects.valueA: Not passed on directly — mutations here are not inherited.
aspects.valueB: Directly passed to offspring — mutations here are heritable.

aspects.label: Examples
aspects.valueA: Skin cells, liver cells, muscle cells.
aspects.valueB: Spermatogonia and oogonia in the testes and ovaries.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Only mutations in germ cells are heritable; somatic mutations (like most cancers) are not passed to children.
overlay.memoryTrick: Germ cells = the 'germ' (origin) of the next generation.
overlay.commonMisconception: 'Germ cells' has nothing to do with germs/microbes — the name refers to 'germination', i.e. origin.
